rationale: The BioSample phenotype attribute carries sex and age only; nothing in the sample record or the ENA study (person-to-person transmission cohort) mentions prematurity or neonatal intensive care, so preterm_nicu is produced by infant age alone. Matches the 47 health_condition rows of this project derived from that attribute (the only other source, external.cmd, gives healthy_control).

All 2,394 health_condition_detail rows of this project store the same phenotype string, which is sex plus age and contains no health or disease text (the field is defined as 'Raw health / disease text'). Judgment call: retire rather than keep a non-health string in a health field; the sex and age values derived from the same string are correct and are not touched.

The BioSample age attribute is a bare number with no unit and no companion unit attribute (16 attributes checked on SAMN04456664/66/704); values span 6-146, so the pipeline's years reading is impossible. The BioProject record states no unit and has no linked publication, and Europe PMC returns 0 hits for PRJNA310878 and SRP069302, so the unit cannot be established. Retires all 21 age values of the project.

evidence_quote: fecal samples from a large cohort of Swedish infants and their mothers
rationale: The ENA study title of PRJEB6456 is verbatim the title of Backhed et al. 2015 ('Dynamics and Stabilization of the Human Gut Microbiome during the First Year of Life'), whose abstract states the cohort is Swedish infants and their mothers. No sample currently has a country; the ENA sample attributes are self-contradictory ('spanish' titles, country 'Denmark', Madrid coordinates), so the project-level paper anchor is used. The paper is not open access, so the locator is a PMID.

The Sex column of the patient table is coded 0/1 with no legend. The header cell reads only 'Sex'; the words sex, gender, male and female do not occur in the article full text, no legend appears in any of the 30 supplementary files (all xlsx/docx/pdf scanned), and BioSample SAMN32957175 carries no sex attribute. The 0/1 semantics are undefined at source, so all 101 sex values are retired.

evidence_quote: Potential of fecal microbiota for early stage detection of colorectal cancer
rationale: The 91 samples whose BioSample diagnosis attribute reads 'Cancer' sit in a colorectal-cancer screening deposit (Zeller et al. 2014); the ENA study title and description identify the cancer. The project's other diagnosis values were checked at the same time and are left alone: 'Small adenoma' (27) and 'Large adenoma' (15) are already colorectal_adenoma, and 'Normal' (66) is healthy_control, consistent with the paper's tumour-free controls.
